ko.title: CNN, 폴리티코 및 MS NOW, 백악관 기자증 발급 금지를 이유로 트럼프 행정부를 상대로 소송 제기

segments.src: ## Three Newsrooms, One Legal Fight
segments.tr: ## 세 개의 뉴스룸, 하나의 법적 싸움

segments.src: CNN, Politico and MS NOW filed a joint lawsuit against the Trump administration this week after the White House revoked press credentials for reporters from all three outlets, cutting off their access to the briefing room, press pool rotations and other official events held on White House grounds.
segments.tr: CNN, 폴리티코 및 MS NOW는 이번 주 트럼프 행정부를 상대로 공동 소송을 제기했습니다. 백악관이 이 세 언론사 소속 기자들의 기자증을 취소하여 브리핑룸 출입, 풀기자단 순번 및 백악관 경내에서 열리는 기타 공식 행사에 대한 접근을 차단했기 때문입니다.

segments.src: The outlets argue in their complaint that stripping credentials from working journalists without a clear, individualized justification violates the First Amendment's protections for a free press, as well as the Fifth Amendment's guarantee of due process.
segments.tr: 이 언론사들은 명확하고 개별적인 정당화 사유 없이 현장 기자들의 자격을 박탈하는 것은 언론의 자유를 보장하는 수정헌법 제1조와 적법절차를 보장하는 수정헌법 제5조를 위반한다고 소장에 명시했습니다.

segments.src: Their filing asks a federal court to restore the reporters' access while the case proceeds and, ultimately, to bar the administration from using credentialing decisions to punish outlets over the content of their coverage.
segments.tr: 이들은 소송이 진행되는 동안 기자들의 출입을 복원하고, 궁극적으로는 행정부가 보도 내용에 대해 언론사를 처벌하기 위해 기자증 발급 결정을 사용하는 것을 금지해 달라고 연방법원에 요청했습니다.

segments.src: ## What the Ban Actually Changed
segments.tr: ## 출입 금지가 실제로 바꾼 것

segments.src: Losing a White House credential is not a symbolic penalty.
segments.tr: 백악관 기자증을 잃는 것은 상징적인 처벌이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It determines whether a reporter can walk into the briefing room, join the small rotating "pool" that travels with the president, or ask a question at a press conference.
segments.tr: 이는 기자가 브리핑룸에 들어갈 수 있는지, 대통령을 수행하는 소규모 순환 "풀(pool)" 기자단에 합류할 수 있는지, 또는 기자회견에서 질문을 할 수 있는지를 결정합니다.

segments.src: For CNN, Politico and MS NOW, the ban means their correspondents now have to rely on pooled footage and reporting from other outlets to cover the presidency — a significant handicap for organizations built around original, on-the-ground reporting.
segments.tr: CNN, 폴리티코, MS NOW에게 이번 출입 금지 조치는 이제 자사 특파원들이 대통령을 취재하기 위해 다른 언론사의 풀 영상과 보도에 의존해야 한다는 것을 의미하며, 이는 독창적인 현장 보도를 중심으로 구축된 언론사들에게는 상당한 핸디캡입니다.

segments.src: The White House has not laid out a detailed public rationale for singling out these three newsrooms.
segments.tr: 백악관은 이 세 뉴스룸을 지목한 데 대한 상세한 공개적 근거를 제시하지 않았습니다.

segments.src: In past disputes over press access, administration officials have generally pointed to conduct during briefings or the tone of an outlet's coverage as justification, arguments that press advocates say amount to viewpoint discrimination dressed up as an access policy.
segments.tr: 과거 언론 접근권을 둘러싼 분쟁에서 행정부 관계자들은 일반적으로 브리핑 중의 행동이나 보도 태도를 정당화 사유로 지적해 왔으나, 언론옹호단체들은 이는 접근권 정책으로 포장된 관점 차별에 해당한다고 주장합니다.

segments.src: ## A Fight the Courts Have Seen Before
segments.tr: ## 법원이 이전에 보았던 싸움

segments.src: This is not the first time a White House has tried to control the press corps by revoking credentials, and history has not been kind to the practice.
segments.tr: 백악관이 기자증을 취소하여 언론단을 통제하려 한 것은 이번이 처음이 아니며, 역사는 이러한 관행에 우호적이지 않았습니다.

segments.src: In 1977, a federal court ruled in *Sherrill v.
segments.tr: 1977년 연방법원은 *Sherrill v.

segments.src: Knight* that the government cannot deny a reporter a White House pass without notice, a reason and a chance to respond — establishing that access, once broadly granted to the press corps, can't be pulled arbitrarily.
segments.tr: Knight* 사건에서 정부가 사전 통지, 이유 및 소명 기회 없이 기자에게 백악관 출입증을 거부할 수 없다고 판결했으며, 이는 언론단에 광범위하게 부여된 접근권이 임의로 철회될 수 없음을 확립했습니다.

segments.src: During Trump's first term, a federal judge sided with CNN in 2018 after correspondent Jim Acosta's credential was suspended, ordering it restored on due-process grounds.
segments.tr: 트럼프의 첫 임기 중인 2018년, 연방 판사는 짐 아코스타(Jim Acosta) 특파원의 기자증이 정지된 후 CNN의 손을 들어주며 적법절차를 근거로 기자증 복원을 명령했습니다.

segments.src: Legal experts note that this precedent puts the administration in a difficult position: courts have consistently held that once the White House opens its doors to the press generally, it cannot then pick and choose which outlets get to walk through them based on how officials feel about their coverage.
segments.tr: 법률 전문가들은 이러한 판례가 행정부를 어려운 입장(difficult position)에 처하게 한다고 지적합니다. 법원은 백악관이 언론 전반에 문을 열어준 이상, 관계자들이 보도에 대해 어떻게 느끼는지에 따라 어떤 언론사가 그 문을 통과할 수 있는지 임의로 선택할 수 없다고 일관되게 판시해 왔습니다.

segments.src: ## The Stakes Beyond Three Newsrooms
segments.tr: ## 세 뉴스룸을 넘어선 이해관계

segments.src: Press freedom organizations, including the Committee to Protect Journalists and the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, have voiced support for the outlets, framing the case as a test of whether any administration can use credentialing as a tool to reward friendly coverage and punish critical reporting.
segments.tr: 언론자유위원회(Committee to Protect Journalists)와 언론자유기자위원회(Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press)를 포함한 언론 자유 단체들은 이 언론사들에 대한 지지를 표명하며, 이번 소송을 어떤 행정부든 우호적인 보도에는 보상을 하고 비판적인 보도에는 처벌을 내리는 도구로 기자증 발급을 이용할 수 있는지 여부를 가늠하는 시험대로 규정했습니다.

segments.src: Other news organizations are watching closely, since a ruling either way could shape how future administrations — of any party — manage access to the White House press corps.
segments.tr: 어떤 쪽으로든 내려질 판결이 향후 어떤 당파의 행정부이든 백악관 언론단에 대한 접근을 관리하는 방식을 형성할 수 있기 때문에, 다른 언론사들도 이를 예의주시하고 있습니다.

segments.src: For now, CNN, Politico and MS NOW say they intend to keep covering the White House using whatever tools remain available to them while the lawsuit moves through the courts.
segments.tr: 현재로서는 CNN, 폴리티코, MS NOW가 소송이 법원을 통해 진행되는 동안 자신들에게 남아 있는 모든 수단을 동원해 백악관 취재를 계속할 의향이라고 밝혔습니다.

segments.src: A hearing date has not yet been set, but legal observers expect the outlets to seek expedited relief given the ongoing impact on their day-to-day coverage.
segments.tr: 심문 기일은 아직 잡히지 않았지만, 법률 관측통들은 일상적인 취재에 미치는 지속적인 영향을 고려할 때 언론사들이 신속한 구제를 모색할 것으로 예상하고 있습니다.

segments.src: *This article summarizes publicly reported developments and is intended for general news information purposes.*
segments.tr: *이 기사는 공개적으로 보도된 발전 상황을 요약한 것이며 일반적인 뉴스 정보 제공을 목적으로 합니다.*

zh.title: CNN、Politico和MS NOW就白宫记者证禁令起诉特朗普政府

segments.src: ## Three Newsrooms, One Legal Fight
segments.tr: ## 三家新闻机构，一场法律诉讼

segments.src: CNN, Politico and MS NOW filed a joint lawsuit against the Trump administration this week after the White House revoked press credentials for reporters from all three outlets, cutting off their access to the briefing room, press pool rotations and other official events held on White House grounds.
segments.tr: 本周，CNN、Politico和MS NOW联合对特朗普政府提起诉讼。此前，白宫撤销了这三家媒体记者的记者证，切断了他们进入简报室、记者团轮换以及白宫内部其他官方活动的权限。

segments.src: The outlets argue in their complaint that stripping credentials from working journalists without a clear, individualized justification violates the First Amendment's protections for a free press, as well as the Fifth Amendment's guarantee of due process.
segments.tr: 这些媒体在诉状中指出，在没有明确、个性化理由的情况下剥夺在职记者的记者证，违反了第一修正案对新闻自由的保护，以及第五修正案对正当程序的保障。

segments.src: Their filing asks a federal court to restore the reporters' access while the case proceeds and, ultimately, to bar the administration from using credentialing decisions to punish outlets over the content of their coverage.
segments.tr: 他们的诉状要求联邦法院在案件审理期间恢复记者的采访权限，并最终禁止政府利用记者证发放决策来惩罚报道内容的媒体。

segments.src: ## What the Ban Actually Changed
segments.tr: ## 禁令究竟改变了什么

segments.src: Losing a White House credential is not a symbolic penalty.
segments.tr: 失去白宫记者证并非象征性的惩罚。

segments.src: It determines whether a reporter can walk into the briefing room, join the small rotating "pool" that travels with the president, or ask a question at a press conference.
segments.tr: 它决定了一名记者是否能够走进简报室、加入随总统出访的轮换“记者团”，或者在新闻发布会上提问。

segments.src: For CNN, Politico and MS NOW, the ban means their correspondents now have to rely on pooled footage and reporting from other outlets to cover the presidency — a significant handicap for organizations built around original, on-the-ground reporting.
segments.tr: 对于CNN、Politico和MS NOW而言，这项禁令意味着他们的记者现在只能依靠其他媒体的素材和报道来报道总统事务——对于以原创、现场报道为基础的机构来说，这是一个巨大的障碍。

segments.src: The White House has not laid out a detailed public rationale for singling out these three newsrooms.
segments.tr: 白宫尚未就单独针对这三家新闻机构给出详细的公开解释。

segments.src: In past disputes over press access, administration officials have generally pointed to conduct during briefings or the tone of an outlet's coverage as justification, arguments that press advocates say amount to viewpoint discrimination dressed up as an access policy.
segments.tr: 在以往关于采访权的争端中，政府官员通常将简报会期间的行为或媒体报道的基调作为合理的借口，而新闻维权人士认为，这些论点无非是披着采访政策外衣的观点歧视。

segments.src: ## A Fight the Courts Have Seen Before
segments.tr: ## 法院已经见过的诉讼

segments.src: This is not the first time a White House has tried to control the press corps by revoking credentials, and history has not been kind to the practice.
segments.tr: 这并非白宫第一次试图通过撤销记者证来控制新闻记者团，而历史对这种做法并不宽容。

segments.src: In 1977, a federal court ruled in *Sherrill v.
segments.tr: 1977年，联邦法院在 *Sherrill v.

segments.src: Knight* that the government cannot deny a reporter a White House pass without notice, a reason and a chance to respond — establishing that access, once broadly granted to the press corps, can't be pulled arbitrarily.
segments.tr: Knight* 案中裁定，政府在没有事先通知、理由和回应机会的情况下，不得拒绝向记者发放白宫通行证——这确立了这样一个原则：一旦广泛授予记者团采访权，就不能随意收回。

segments.src: During Trump's first term, a federal judge sided with CNN in 2018 after correspondent Jim Acosta's credential was suspended, ordering it restored on due-process grounds.
segments.tr: 在特朗普的第一任期内，记者吉姆·阿科斯塔（Jim Acosta）的记者证被暂停后，联邦法官在2018年站在了CNN一边，下令以正当程序为由恢复其记者证。

segments.src: Legal experts note that this precedent puts the administration in a difficult position: courts have consistently held that once the White House opens its doors to the press generally, it cannot then pick and choose which outlets get to walk through them based on how officials feel about their coverage.
segments.tr: 法律专家指出，这一先例使政府陷入了困境：法院一再认为，一旦白宫向媒体普遍敞开大门，就不能再根据官员对报道的感受，挑选哪些媒体可以进入。

segments.src: ## The Stakes Beyond Three Newsrooms
segments.tr: ## 三家新闻机构之外的利害关系

segments.src: Press freedom organizations, including the Committee to Protect Journalists and the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, have voiced support for the outlets, framing the case as a test of whether any administration can use credentialing as a tool to reward friendly coverage and punish critical reporting.
segments.tr: 包括保护记者委员会和记者新闻自由委员会在内的新闻自由组织对这些媒体表示支持，将此案视为对任何政府是否能利用记者证作为奖励友好报道、惩罚批评性报道工具的考验。

segments.src: Other news organizations are watching closely, since a ruling either way could shape how future administrations — of any party — manage access to the White House press corps.
segments.tr: 其他新闻机构正在密切关注，因为无论哪一方的裁决都可能影响未来任何党派的政府如何管理白宫记者团的采访权。

segments.src: For now, CNN, Politico and MS NOW say they intend to keep covering the White House using whatever tools remain available to them while the lawsuit moves through the courts.
segments.tr: 目前，CNN、Politico和MS NOW表示，在诉讼通过法院审理期间，他们打算利用手头所有可用的工具继续报道白宫。

segments.src: A hearing date has not yet been set, but legal observers expect the outlets to seek expedited relief given the ongoing impact on their day-to-day coverage.
segments.tr: 听证会日期尚未确定，但法律观察人士预计，鉴于对日常报道的持续影响，这些媒体将寻求加速救济。

segments.tr: *本文总结了公开报道的发展情况，仅供一般新闻信息参考。*

es.title: CNN, Politico y MS NOW demandan a la administración Trump por la prohibición de credenciales de prensa en la Casa Blanca

segments.src: ## Three Newsrooms, One Legal Fight
segments.tr: ## Tres redacciones, una batalla legal

segments.src: CNN, Politico and MS NOW filed a joint lawsuit against the Trump administration this week after the White House revoked press credentials for reporters from all three outlets, cutting off their access to the briefing room, press pool rotations and other official events held on White House grounds.
segments.tr: CNN, Politico y MS NOW presentaron una demanda conjunta contra la administración Trump esta semana después de que la Casa Blanca revocara las credenciales de prensa de los reporteros de los tres medios, cortando su acceso a la sala de prensa, a las rotaciones del grupo de prensa y a otros eventos oficiales celebrados en los terrenos de la Casa Blanca.

segments.src: The outlets argue in their complaint that stripping credentials from working journalists without a clear, individualized justification violates the First Amendment's protections for a free press, as well as the Fifth Amendment's guarantee of due process.
segments.tr: Los medios argumentan en su demanda que retirar las credenciales a periodistas en activo sin una justificación clara e individualizada viola las protecciones de la Primera Enmienda para una prensa libre, así como la garantía del debido proceso de la Quinta Enmienda.

segments.src: Their filing asks a federal court to restore the reporters' access while the case proceeds and, ultimately, to bar the administration from using credentialing decisions to punish outlets over the content of their coverage.
segments.tr: Su presentación solicita a un tribunal federal que restablezca el acceso de los reporteros mientras el caso avanza y, en última instancia, que prohíba a la administración utilizar las decisiones sobre credenciales para castigar a los medios por el contenido de su cobertura.

segments.src: ## What the Ban Actually Changed
segments.tr: ## Lo que realmente cambió la prohibición

segments.src: Losing a White House credential is not a symbolic penalty.
segments.tr: Perder una credencial de la Casa Blanca no es una sanción simbólica.

segments.src: It determines whether a reporter can walk into the briefing room, join the small rotating "pool" that travels with the president, or ask a question at a press conference.
segments.tr: Determina si un reportero puede entrar en la sala de prensa, unirse al pequeño "grupo" rotativo que viaja con el presidente o hacer una pregunta en una conferencia de prensa.

segments.src: For CNN, Politico and MS NOW, the ban means their correspondents now have to rely on pooled footage and reporting from other outlets to cover the presidency — a significant handicap for organizations built around original, on-the-ground reporting.
segments.tr: Para CNN, Politico y MS NOW, la prohibición significa que sus corresponsales ahora tienen que depender de imágenes y reportajes compartidos de otros medios para cubrir la presidencia, una desventaja significativa para organizaciones construidas en torno a reportajes originales y sobre el terreno.

segments.src: The White House has not laid out a detailed public rationale for singling out these three newsrooms.
segments.tr: La Casa Blanca no ha expuesto una justificación pública detallada para señalar a estas tres redacciones.

segments.src: In past disputes over press access, administration officials have generally pointed to conduct during briefings or the tone of an outlet's coverage as justification, arguments that press advocates say amount to viewpoint discrimination dressed up as an access policy.
segments.tr: En disputas pasadas sobre el acceso a la prensa, los funcionarios de la administración generalmente han señalado la conducta durante las sesiones informativas o el tono de la cobertura de un medio como justificación, argumentos que los defensores de la prensa dicen que equivalen a una discriminación de puntos de vista disfrazada de política de acceso.

segments.src: ## A Fight the Courts Have Seen Before
segments.tr: ## Una pelea que los tribunales ya han visto antes

segments.src: This is not the first time a White House has tried to control the press corps by revoking credentials, and history has not been kind to the practice.
segments.tr: Esta no es la primera vez que una Casa Blanca intenta controlar al cuerpo de prensa revocando credenciales, y la historia no ha sido amable con esta práctica.

segments.src: In 1977, a federal court ruled in *Sherrill v.
segments.tr: En 1977, un tribunal federal dictaminó en el caso *Sherrill v.

segments.src: Knight* that the government cannot deny a reporter a White House pass without notice, a reason and a chance to respond — establishing that access, once broadly granted to the press corps, can't be pulled arbitrarily.
segments.tr: Knight* que el gobierno no puede negar a un reportero un pase de la Casa Blanca sin previo aviso, una razón y una oportunidad para responder, estableciendo que el acceso, una vez otorgado ampliamente al cuerpo de prensa, no puede ser retirado arbitrariamente.

segments.src: During Trump's first term, a federal judge sided with CNN in 2018 after correspondent Jim Acosta's credential was suspended, ordering it restored on due-process grounds.
segments.tr: Durante el primer mandato de Trump, un juez federal falló a favor de la CNN en 2018 después de que la credencial del corresponsal Jim Acosta fuera suspendida, ordenando su restauración por motivos de debido proceso.

segments.src: Legal experts note that this precedent puts the administration in a difficult position: courts have consistently held that once the White House opens its doors to the press generally, it cannot then pick and choose which outlets get to walk through them based on how officials feel about their coverage.
segments.tr: Los expertos legales señalan que este precedente coloca a la administración en una posición difícil: los tribunales han sostenido constantemente que una vez que la Casa Blanca abre sus puertas a la prensa en general, no puede entonces elegir qué medios pueden entrar basándose en cómo se sienten los funcionarios sobre su cobertura.

segments.src: ## The Stakes Beyond Three Newsrooms
segments.tr: ## Lo que está en juego más allá de tres redacciones

segments.src: Press freedom organizations, including the Committee to Protect Journalists and the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, have voiced support for the outlets, framing the case as a test of whether any administration can use credentialing as a tool to reward friendly coverage and punish critical reporting.
segments.tr: Organizaciones de libertad de prensa, incluido el Comité para la Protección de los Periodistas y el Comité de Reporteros por la Libertad de Prensa, han expresado su apoyo a los medios, enmarcando el caso como una prueba de si alguna administración puede utilizar la acreditación como una herramienta para recompensar la cobertura amistosa y castigar los reportajes críticos.

segments.src: Other news organizations are watching closely, since a ruling either way could shape how future administrations — of any party — manage access to the White House press corps.
segments.tr: Otros medios de comunicación están observando de cerca, ya que un fallo en cualquier dirección podría dar forma a cómo las futuras administraciones, de cualquier partido, gestionan el acceso al cuerpo de prensa de la Casa Blanca.

segments.src: For now, CNN, Politico and MS NOW say they intend to keep covering the White House using whatever tools remain available to them while the lawsuit moves through the courts.
segments.tr: Por ahora, CNN, Politico y MS NOW dicen que tienen la intención de seguir cubriendo la Casa Blanca utilizando las herramientas que les queden disponibles mientras la demanda avanza por los tribunales.

segments.src: A hearing date has not yet been set, but legal observers expect the outlets to seek expedited relief given the ongoing impact on their day-to-day coverage.
segments.tr: Aún no se ha fijado una fecha para la audiencia, pero los observadores legales esperan que los medios busquen una medida cautelar acelerada dado el impacto continuo en su cobertura diaria.

segments.tr: ## Trois rédactions, un combat juridique

segments.src: CNN, Politico and MS NOW filed a joint lawsuit against the Trump administration this week after the White House revoked press credentials for reporters from all three outlets, cutting off their access to the briefing room, press pool rotations and other official events held on White House grounds.
segments.tr: CNN, Politico et MS NOW ont déposé une plainte commune contre l'administration Trump cette semaine après que la Maison-Blanche a révoqué les accréditations de presse des journalistes de ces trois médias, leur coupant ainsi l'accès à la salle de presse, aux rotations du pool de presse et aux autres événements officiels organisés dans l'enceinte de la Maison-Blanche.

segments.src: The outlets argue in their complaint that stripping credentials from working journalists without a clear, individualized justification violates the First Amendment's protections for a free press, as well as the Fifth Amendment's guarantee of due process.
segments.tr: Dans leur plainte, les médias soutiennent que le retrait des accréditations de journalistes en activité sans justification claire et individualisée viole les protections du premier amendement en faveur d'une presse libre, ainsi que la garantie de procédure régulière du cinquième amendement.

segments.src: Their filing asks a federal court to restore the reporters' access while the case proceeds and, ultimately, to bar the administration from using credentialing decisions to punish outlets over the content of their coverage.
segments.tr: Leur dossier demande à un tribunal fédéral de rétablir l'accès des journalistes pendant que l'affaire suit son cours et, en fin de compte, d'interdire à l'administration d'utiliser les décisions d'accréditation pour punir les médias en raison du contenu de leur couverture.

segments.src: ## What the Ban Actually Changed
segments.tr: ## Ce que l'interdiction a réellement changé

segments.src: Losing a White House credential is not a symbolic penalty.
segments.tr: Perdre une accréditation de la Maison-Blanche n'est pas une sanction symbolique.

segments.src: It determines whether a reporter can walk into the briefing room, join the small rotating "pool" that travels with the president, or ask a question at a press conference.
segments.tr: Cela détermine si un journaliste peut entrer dans la salle de presse, rejoindre le petit « pool » rotatif qui voyage avec le président ou poser une question lors d'une conférence de presse.

segments.src: For CNN, Politico and MS NOW, the ban means their correspondents now have to rely on pooled footage and reporting from other outlets to cover the presidency — a significant handicap for organizations built around original, on-the-ground reporting.
segments.tr: Pour CNN, Politico et MS NOW, l'interdiction signifie que leurs correspondants doivent désormais s'appuyer sur les images et les reportages d'autres médias pour couvrir la présidence — un handicap important pour des organisations fondées sur des reportages originaux et de terrain.

segments.src: The White House has not laid out a detailed public rationale for singling out these three newsrooms.
segments.tr: La Maison-Blanche n'a pas exposé de justification publique détaillée pour avoir ciblé ces trois rédactions.

segments.src: In past disputes over press access, administration officials have generally pointed to conduct during briefings or the tone of an outlet's coverage as justification, arguments that press advocates say amount to viewpoint discrimination dressed up as an access policy.
segments.tr: Lors de précédents différends sur l'accès à la presse, les responsables de l'administration ont généralement invoqué la conduite lors des briefings ou le ton de la couverture d'un média comme justification, des arguments que les défenseurs de la presse considèrent comme une discrimination fondée sur les opinions, déguisée en politique d'accès.

segments.src: ## A Fight the Courts Have Seen Before
segments.tr: ## Un combat que les tribunaux ont déjà connu

segments.src: This is not the first time a White House has tried to control the press corps by revoking credentials, and history has not been kind to the practice.
segments.tr: Ce n'est pas la première fois qu'une Maison-Blanche tente de contrôler le corps de presse en révoquant des accréditations, et l'histoire n'a pas été tendre avec cette pratique.

segments.src: In 1977, a federal court ruled in *Sherrill v.
segments.tr: En 1977, un tribunal fédéral a statué dans l'affaire *Sherrill c.

segments.src: Knight* that the government cannot deny a reporter a White House pass without notice, a reason and a chance to respond — establishing that access, once broadly granted to the press corps, can't be pulled arbitrarily.
segments.tr: Knight* que le gouvernement ne peut pas refuser à un journaliste un laissez-passer pour la Maison-Blanche sans préavis, sans motif et sans possibilité de réponse — établissant que l'accès, une fois largement accordé au corps de presse, ne peut être retiré arbitrairement.

segments.src: During Trump's first term, a federal judge sided with CNN in 2018 after correspondent Jim Acosta's credential was suspended, ordering it restored on due-process grounds.
segments.tr: Pendant le premier mandat de Trump, un juge fédéral a donné raison à CNN en 2018 après la suspension de l'accréditation du correspondant Jim Acosta, ordonnant son rétablissement pour des raisons de procédure régulière.

segments.src: Legal experts note that this precedent puts the administration in a difficult position: courts have consistently held that once the White House opens its doors to the press generally, it cannot then pick and choose which outlets get to walk through them based on how officials feel about their coverage.
segments.tr: Les experts juridiques notent que ce précédent place l'administration dans une position difficile : les tribunaux ont constamment soutenu qu'une fois que la Maison-Blanche ouvre ses portes à la presse en général, elle ne peut pas choisir quels médias peuvent les franchir en fonction de ce que les responsables pensent de leur couverture.

segments.src: ## The Stakes Beyond Three Newsrooms
segments.tr: ## Les enjeux au-delà de ces trois rédactions

segments.src: Press freedom organizations, including the Committee to Protect Journalists and the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, have voiced support for the outlets, framing the case as a test of whether any administration can use credentialing as a tool to reward friendly coverage and punish critical reporting.
segments.tr: Des organisations de défense de la liberté de la presse, dont le Committee to Protect Journalists et le Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, ont exprimé leur soutien aux médias, présentant l'affaire comme un test pour savoir si une administration peut utiliser l'accréditation comme un outil pour récompenser une couverture amicale et punir les reportages critiques.

segments.src: Other news organizations are watching closely, since a ruling either way could shape how future administrations — of any party — manage access to the White House press corps.
segments.tr: D'autres organisations de presse observent la situation de près, car une décision dans un sens ou dans l'autre pourrait façonner la manière dont les futures administrations — quel que soit leur parti — gèrent l'accès au corps de presse de la Maison-Blanche.

segments.src: For now, CNN, Politico and MS NOW say they intend to keep covering the White House using whatever tools remain available to them while the lawsuit moves through the courts.
segments.tr: Pour l'instant, CNN, Politico et MS NOW déclarent qu'ils ont l'intention de continuer à couvrir la Maison-Blanche en utilisant tous les outils qui leur restent disponibles pendant que la plainte suit son cours devant les tribunaux.

segments.src: A hearing date has not yet been set, but legal observers expect the outlets to seek expedited relief given the ongoing impact on their day-to-day coverage.
segments.tr: Aucune date d'audience n'a encore été fixée, mais les observateurs juridiques s'attendent à ce que les médias demandent une procédure accélérée compte tenu de l'impact continu sur leur couverture quotidienne.

segments.tr: Em disputas passadas sobre o acesso da imprensa, autoridades da administração geralmente apontaram a conduta durante as coletivas ou o tom da cobertura de um veículo como justificativa, argumentos que defensores da imprensa dizem equivaler a discriminação de ponto de vista disfarçada de política de acesso.

segments.src: ## A Fight the Courts Have Seen Before
segments.tr: ## Uma Luta que os Tribunais Já Viram Antes

segments.src: This is not the first time a White House has tried to control the press corps by revoking credentials, and history has not been kind to the practice.
segments.tr: Esta não é a primeira vez que a Casa Branca tenta controlar o corpo de imprensa revogando credenciais, e a história não tem sido gentil com essa prática.

segments.src: In 1977, a federal court ruled in *Sherrill v.
segments.tr: Em 1977, um tribunal federal decidiu em *Sherrill v.

segments.src: Knight* that the government cannot deny a reporter a White House pass without notice, a reason and a chance to respond — establishing that access, once broadly granted to the press corps, can't be pulled arbitrarily.
segments.tr: Knight* que o governo não pode negar a um repórter um passe para a Casa Branca sem aviso prévio, um motivo e uma chance de responder — estabelecendo que o acesso, uma vez concedido amplamente ao corpo de imprensa, não pode ser retirado arbitrariamente.

segments.src: Legal experts note that this precedent puts the administration in a difficult position: courts have consistently held that once the White House opens its doors to the press generally, it cannot then pick and choose which outlets get to walk through them based on how officials feel about their coverage.
segments.tr: Especialistas jurídicos observam que esse precedente coloca a administração em uma posição difícil: os tribunais têm sustentado consistentemente que, uma vez que a Casa Branca abre suas portas para a imprensa em geral, ela não pode então escolher quais veículos podem passar por elas com base no que as autoridades acham de sua cobertura.

segments.src: ## The Stakes Beyond Three Newsrooms

segments.tr: Organizações de liberdade de imprensa, incluindo o Comitê para a Proteção dos Jornalistas e o Comitê de Repórteres pela Liberdade de Imprensa, manifestaram apoio aos veículos, enquadrando o caso como um teste de se qualquer administração pode usar o credenciamento como uma ferramenta para recompensar cobertura amigável e punir reportagens críticas.

segments.src: The White House has not laid out a detailed public rationale for singling out these three newsrooms.
segments.tr: Gedung Putih belum memaparkan alasan publik yang terperinci untuk memilih ketiga ruang redaksi ini.

segments.tr: Dalam perselisihan masa lalu tentang akses pers, pejabat pemerintah umumnya menunjuk pada perilaku selama briefing atau nada liputan outlet sebagai pembenaran, argumen yang dikatakan para advokat pers sama dengan diskriminasi sudut pandang yang disamarkan sebagai kebijakan akses.

segments.src: ## A Fight the Courts Have Seen Before
segments.tr: ## Pertarungan yang Pernah Dilihat Pengadilan Sebelumnya

segments.src: This is not the first time a White House has tried to control the press corps by revoking credentials, and history has not been kind to the practice.
segments.tr: Ini bukan pertama kalinya Gedung Putih mencoba mengendalikan korps pers dengan mencabut kredensial, dan sejarah tidak baik pada praktik tersebut.

segments.src: In 1977, a federal court ruled in *Sherrill v.
segments.tr: Pada tahun 1977, sebuah pengadilan federal memutuskan dalam *Sherrill v.

segments.src: Knight* that the government cannot deny a reporter a White House pass without notice, a reason and a chance to respond — establishing that access, once broadly granted to the press corps, can't be pulled arbitrarily.
segments.tr: Knight* bahwa pemerintah tidak dapat menolak izin Gedung Putih kepada seorang wartawan tanpa pemberitahuan, alasan, dan kesempatan untuk menanggapi — menetapkan bahwa akses, begitu diberikan secara luas kepada korps pers, tidak dapat dicabut secara sewenang-wenang.

segments.src: During Trump's first term, a federal judge sided with CNN in 2018 after correspondent Jim Acosta's credential was suspended, ordering it restored on due-process grounds.
segments.tr: Selama masa jabatan pertama Trump, seorang hakim federal memihak CNN pada tahun 2018 setelah kredensial koresponden Jim Acosta ditangguhkan, memerintahkan pemulihannya atas dasar proses hukum yang adil.

segments.src: Legal experts note that this precedent puts the administration in a difficult position: courts have consistently held that once the White House opens its doors to the press generally, it cannot then pick and choose which outlets get to walk through them based on how officials feel about their coverage.
segments.tr: Pakar hukum mencatat bahwa preseden ini menempatkan pemerintah dalam posisi yang sulit: pengadilan secara konsisten berpendapat bahwa begitu Gedung Putih membukakan pintu bagi pers secara umum, ia tidak dapat kemudian memilih outlet mana yang dapat berjalan melalui mereka berdasarkan bagaimana perasaan para pejabat tentang liputan mereka.

segments.src: ## The Stakes Beyond Three Newsrooms

segments.tr: Organisasi kebebasan pers, termasuk Committee to Protect Journalists dan Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, telah menyuarakan dukungan untuk outlet tersebut, membingkai kasus ini sebagai ujian apakah ada administrasi yang dapat menggunakan kredensial sebagai alat untuk menghiaih liputan yang ramah dan menghukum pelaporan yang kritis.

segments.src: Other news organizations are watching closely, since a ruling either way could shape how future administrations — of any party — manage access to the White House press corps.

segments.src: For now, CNN, Politico and MS NOW say they intend to keep covering the White House using whatever tools remain available to them while the lawsuit moves through the courts.

segments.src: A hearing date has not yet been set, but legal observers expect the outlets to seek expedited relief given the ongoing impact on their day-to-day coverage.

de.title: CNN, Politico und MS NOW verklagen die Trump-Regierung wegen Entzugs der Presseakkreditierung für das Weiße Haus

segments.src: ## Three Newsrooms, One Legal Fight
segments.tr: ## Drei Nachrichtenredaktionen, ein Rechtsstreit

segments.src: CNN, Politico and MS NOW filed a joint lawsuit against the Trump administration this week after the White House revoked press credentials for reporters from all three outlets, cutting off their access to the briefing room, press pool rotations and other official events held on White House grounds.
segments.tr: CNN, Politico und MS NOW haben diese Woche eine gemeinsame Klage gegen die Trump-Regierung eingereicht, nachdem das Weiße Haus die Presseakkreditierungen für Reporter aller drei Medienhäuser widerrufen hatte. Damit wurde ihnen der Zugang zum Briefing-Raum, zu den rotierenden Presseteams und zu anderen offiziellen Veranstaltungen auf dem Gelände des Weißen Hauses verwehrt.

segments.src: The outlets argue in their complaint that stripping credentials from working journalists without a clear, individualized justification violates the First Amendment's protections for a free press, as well as the Fifth Amendment's guarantee of due process.
segments.tr: Die Medienhäuser argumentieren in ihrer Klageschrift, dass der Entzug von Akkreditierungen bei arbeitenden Journalisten ohne eine klare, individuelle Begründung die durch den ersten Verfassungszusatz (First Amendment) geschützte Pressefreiheit sowie das durch den fünften Verfassungszusatz (Fifth Amendment) garantierte Recht auf ein ordnungsgemäßes Verfahren (Due Process) verletzt.

segments.src: Their filing asks a federal court to restore the reporters' access while the case proceeds and, ultimately, to bar the administration from using credentialing decisions to punish outlets over the content of their coverage.
segments.tr: Ihr Antrag fordert ein Bundesgericht auf, den Zugang der Reporter während des laufenden Verfahrens wiederherzustellen und der Regierung letztendlich zu untersagen, Entscheidungen über Akkreditierungen als Mittel zu nutzen, um Medienhäuser für den Inhalt ihrer Berichterstattung zu bestrafen.

segments.src: ## What the Ban Actually Changed
segments.tr: ## Was das Verbot tatsächlich bewirkte

segments.src: Losing a White House credential is not a symbolic penalty.
segments.tr: Der Verlust einer Akkreditierung für das Weiße Haus ist keine symbolische Strafe.

segments.src: It determines whether a reporter can walk into the briefing room, join the small rotating "pool" that travels with the president, or ask a question at a press conference.
segments.tr: Sie bestimmt, ob ein Reporter den Briefing-Raum betreten, sich dem kleinen rotierenden "Pool" anschließen kann, der mit dem Präsidenten reist, oder auf einer Pressekonferenz eine Frage stellen darf.

segments.src: For CNN, Politico and MS NOW, the ban means their correspondents now have to rely on pooled footage and reporting from other outlets to cover the presidency — a significant handicap for organizations built around original, on-the-ground reporting.
segments.tr: Für CNN, Politico und MS NOW bedeutet das Verbot, dass ihre Korrespondenten nun auf das Bildmaterial und die Berichterstattung anderer Medien angewiesen sind, um über die Präsidentschaft zu berichten – ein erheblicher Nachteil für Organisationen, deren Arbeit auf originärer Berichterstattung vor Ort basiert.

segments.src: The White House has not laid out a detailed public rationale for singling out these three newsrooms.
segments.tr: Das Weiße Haus hat keine detaillierte öffentliche Begründung dafür geliefert, warum gerade diese drei Nachrichtenredaktionen ausgewählt wurden.

segments.src: In past disputes over press access, administration officials have generally pointed to conduct during briefings or the tone of an outlet's coverage as justification, arguments that press advocates say amount to viewpoint discrimination dressed up as an access policy.
segments.tr: Bei früheren Streitigkeiten über den Zugang der Presse verwiesen Regierungsvertreter im Allgemeinen auf das Verhalten während der Briefings oder den Ton der Berichterstattung eines Medienhauses als Rechtfertigung – Argumente, die laut Pressevertretern einer Diskriminierung aufgrund der Ansichten gleichkommen, die als Zugangspolitik getarnt wird.

segments.src: ## A Fight the Courts Have Seen Before
segments.tr: ## Ein Kampf, den die Gerichte schon kennen

segments.src: This is not the first time a White House has tried to control the press corps by revoking credentials, and history has not been kind to the practice.
segments.tr: Dies ist nicht das erste Mal, dass ein Weißes Haus versucht, das Pressekorps durch den Widerruf von Akkreditierungen zu kontrollieren, und die Geschichte war mit dieser Praxis nicht gnädig.

segments.src: In 1977, a federal court ruled in *Sherrill v.
segments.tr: Im Jahr 1977 entschied ein Bundesgericht im Fall *Sherrill v.

segments.src: Knight* that the government cannot deny a reporter a White House pass without notice, a reason and a chance to respond — establishing that access, once broadly granted to the press corps, can't be pulled arbitrarily.
segments.tr: Knight*, dass die Regierung einem Reporter den Presseausweis für das Weiße Haus nicht ohne Vorankündigung, Begründung und die Möglichkeit zur Stellungnahme verweigern darf – womit festgestellt wurde, dass der Zugang, sobald er dem Pressekorps allgemein gewährt wurde, nicht willkürlich entzogen werden kann.

segments.src: During Trump's first term, a federal judge sided with CNN in 2018 after correspondent Jim Acosta's credential was suspended, ordering it restored on due-process grounds.
segments.tr: Während Trumps erster Amtszeit gab ein Bundesrichter 2018 CNN recht, nachdem die Akkreditierung des Korrespondenten Jim Acosta ausgesetzt worden war, und ordnete deren Wiederherstellung aufgrund des Rechts auf ein ordnungsgemäßes Verfahren an.

segments.src: Legal experts note that this precedent puts the administration in a difficult position: courts have consistently held that once the White House opens its doors to the press generally, it cannot then pick and choose which outlets get to walk through them based on how officials feel about their coverage.
segments.tr: Rechtsexperten merken an, dass dieser Präzedenzfall die Regierung in eine schwierige Lage bringt: Gerichte haben konsequent entschieden, dass das Weiße Haus, sobald es seine Türen generell für die Presse öffnet, nicht nach Belieben auswählen darf, welche Medienhäuser diese passieren dürfen, basierend darauf, wie Regierungsvertreter über deren Berichterstattung denken.

segments.src: ## The Stakes Beyond Three Newsrooms
segments.tr: ## Mehr als nur drei Nachrichtenredaktionen betroffen

segments.src: Press freedom organizations, including the Committee to Protect Journalists and the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, have voiced support for the outlets, framing the case as a test of whether any administration can use credentialing as a tool to reward friendly coverage and punish critical reporting.
segments.tr: Organisationen für Pressefreiheit, darunter das Committee to Protect Journalists und das Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, haben ihre Unterstützung für die Medienhäuser bekundet und den Fall als Test dafür bezeichnet, ob eine Regierung Akkreditierungen als Instrument nutzen kann, um wohlwollende Berichterstattung zu belohnen und kritische Berichterstattung zu bestrafen.

segments.src: Other news organizations are watching closely, since a ruling either way could shape how future administrations — of any party — manage access to the White House press corps.
segments.tr: Andere Nachrichtenorganisationen beobachten die Situation genau, da ein Urteil in die eine oder andere Richtung beeinflussen könnte, wie zukünftige Regierungen – egal welcher Partei – den Zugang zum Pressekorps des Weißen Hauses handhaben.

segments.src: For now, CNN, Politico and MS NOW say they intend to keep covering the White House using whatever tools remain available to them while the lawsuit moves through the courts.
segments.tr: Vorerst erklären CNN, Politico und MS NOW, dass sie beabsichtigen, weiterhin über das Weiße Haus zu berichten, indem sie alle ihnen verbleibenden Mittel nutzen, während die Klage die Gerichte durchläuft.

segments.src: A hearing date has not yet been set, but legal observers expect the outlets to seek expedited relief given the ongoing impact on their day-to-day coverage.
segments.tr: Ein Termin für eine Anhörung wurde noch nicht festgelegt, aber Rechtsbeobachter erwarten, dass die Medienhäuser angesichts der laufenden Auswirkungen auf ihre tägliche Berichterstattung ein beschleunigtes Verfahren beantragen werden.
